title: title and description metadata
learningObjectives: Explain title and description metadata and choose appropriate document or embedded-resource metadata.

understand.concept: The document title element provides the page title shown in browser tabs, history, and other contexts. A meta description can provide a short summary that search engines may use as a search result snippet, but it does not guarantee that exact text will be displayed.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear titles help users identify pages across tabs and bookmarks. Descriptions should accurately summarise page content and avoid keyword stuffing or misleading claims.
understand.analogy: The title is the name on the page's folder; the description is a short note explaining what the folder contains.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; metadata and embedding behaviour follow browser, HTTP, and search-engine processing rules.

explain.narrative: The title names the document, and the description provides a concise summary. Search engines may choose other text for a result snippet.

examples.code: <head><title>HTML Forms — CodeSaathi</title><meta name='description' content='Learn accessible HTML forms, labels, input types, and native validation with practical examples.'></head>
examples.explanation: The title names the document, and the description provides a concise summary. Search engines may choose other text for a result snippet.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered or document-head example demonstrating the HTML feature.

practise.guidedTask: Write a unique title and accurate description for a lesson page. Ensure the title makes sense when shown outside the website.
practise.independentTask: Prepare a document head or embed example. Check accessibility, security permissions, and whether metadata accurately describes the content.
hints: Use absolute canonical URLs when declaring a canonical target.
Never treat crawler directives as access control.
Use restrictive iframe permissions and a meaningful title.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>title and description metadata</title></head><body>
<head><title>HTML Forms — CodeSaathi</title><meta name='description' content='Learn accessible HTML forms, labels, input types, and native validation with practical examples.'></head>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What does the HTML title element primarily provide?
options: The document's title for browser and navigation contexts
questions.answer: The document's title for browser and navigation contexts
questions.explanation: The document title is used in browser tabs, history, and other contexts.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide metadata and embedding?
options: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
Use metadata as a substitute for authentication
Grant every embedded document all permissions
questions.answer: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate and embedded resources should receive only necessary capabilities.
